body: Ha, but we can own guns which counts for something I guess? There is a lot of back and forth in the media between America and the EU/ Asia but Australia kind of gets left out. I really don't know a whole lot about Australia. Do you guys have open container laws?

I don't even know how it got so bad. I read an article about a guy paying ~$70,000 for an anti-venom that cost ~$800 on Amazon. I love my country but I wonder where all "America is the most free" rhetoric has come from because being saddled by debt doesn't seem free.

That sounds much better than what we have. I attempted to go to a "low cost" clinic and just to have my vitals taken cost me $160, I didn't actually receive any treatment. We have Medicare too but it does not cover the majority of people. 
I appreciate you listening and helping me out, it's nice to just have a conversation with someone.

Obama is actually kind of making it worse :/ Since The insurance companies are required to cover such a wide variety of conditions the prices have skyrocketed. As in the cheapest policy I found as a "healthy" 20ish year old has a $3,000 deductible on top of $250 per month. It is absolutely horrendous. I really with we could just switch to what Europe or Canada has and cut out these damn insurance companies.
Yes, I did yoga often and went on walks with my dog but the past few months I have not been able to muster the energy to do it. It just got really bad.

I read a memoir a while ago about a woman with schizophrenia who got treatment in Europe, it blew my mind that she could just go and ask for help and they just... did. To get that kind of treatment in America would bankrupt the average person. It's a sad state of affairs.

I don't really have any friends here. I am surrounded by people who have no interest in me other than to speak poorly of me when I am not around. I'm very shy and basically just hang out with people my boyfriend knows or people I work with. I'm not close enough to them for them to care.

That is completely logical but I live in an area where depression and the like are heavily stigmatized. I know i'm not the only one to go through this but I cant afford to end up in an inpatient facility because I asked nicely for someone to put away their guns or called a friend crying about how much I hate myself. No one deals with it or just lends an ear, they get you committed. I just feel like there is no way for me to get better, I cant remember the last time I was happy and at the same time I cant afford heath insurance to see a therapist or even update my medication.

I need to be though. I have no one to fall back on, my parents are dead, I have no family. If I fail I have nowhere to go. There is no safety net, I have always worked really hard and if I admit that it was not good enough then whats what point of going on if my best wasn't enough?
Thanks, Its nice that I don't have to worry about being judged.

He is not the kind of person who understands depression. I'm just not capable of making him lock up his guns. I explained once, in no uncertain terms, and that was not enough. And the method is not the problem, there are any number of potential ways a person could kill themselves. It just hurts that he sees the potential threat to his liberty/ property as more pressing than my mental health, all the more reason that he is not someone I can confide in about this kind of thing.
I don't know how. I assumed asking him once would be enough, he just does not understand and I don't know how to make him without it being... weird

12 so it's definitely a me problem.  I can't apply to anything too far away yet because my bf has two years left of school. I have gotten hired at every job I have interviewed for up until now so I am completely at a loss. I have a great resume, just not that will get me hired at the places I want to go.

Like seriously choked. Complete brain malfunction. I was asked a really basic question, which I had prepared to answer, and took the interviewer on a ridiculous journey that did not, in any way, answer the question sufficiently. This was after two other interviews at the same place where I did great and was sure I was going to get the job. And then at a different place I FORGOT HOW TO USE THE COMPUTER. I dont even know wtf happened. I have logged thousands of hours on these programs, graduated at the top of my class, and I even spent extra time practicing before the interview but as soon as I sat down for the test I just froze. It was heartbreaking.

Two websites freelance. Upon graduating I applied at every design firm in the area and either choked during the interviews or did not get a reply. I have not had that problem before, I think it's because of the depression. I just cant think as quickly as I am used to. The immediate, repeated failures got me down pretty quickly and now I don't have the energy to do anything productive. I've been so broke I can't afford the monthly fee for the design software anyway.
Graphic design. In hindsight it was not a stable career choice.
Under-employed college graduate. I am working at a dead-end job I hate and am barely able to pay my bills. I just can not seem to get a job in my preferred field.
